newsitem.title: USA: Utah residents protest Clinton decision.
newsitem.headline: Utah residents protest Clinton decision.

text.p: Residents in Kanab, Utah, Wednesday closed down their small town for an afternoon to protest President Clinton's decision to create the largest national monument in the continental United States.

Calling the area "some of the most remarkable land in the world," the president signed an order that ends new land development on 1.7 million acres (690,000 hectares) of federal land in southern Utah.
While the move is sure to be a hit with environmentalists, it was not warmly greeted in the region most affected.
The Kane County Commission said the decision makes no economic sense in light of America's dependency on foreign oil.
Of the 1 billion tons of coal produced annually in the United States, 80 percent is used to fuel electric utilities.
Flags in the town were flown at half-staff. Business and city government offices closed for the afternoon and students were released from school to attend the rally.
People in the town of about 3,300 fear that about 900 jobs promised by a coal mining company will be lost because the monument will be an environmentally protected area.

Fifty black balloons - representing the 50 U.S. states - were released to symbolise what residents believe is the loss of rights that other states may suffer by being left out of the deicison making process.
